title: Introduction to Tangliengim
content:
繁體中文
简体中文

Tangliengim (東寧音당ˉ롕임ˆ) is a sound-based writing system for Hokkien. Its name means “the sounds of Tanglieng,” with 音임ˆ pointing to its focus on pronunciation, tone, and tone sandhi, whilst echoing Hunminjeongeum (訓民正音), the original name of Hangul.

It is mainly used in mixed Hanri-Hangul writing, where Hanri (Hokkien written in Chinese characters) carries the character-based layer and Hangul clarifies sound. Pure Hangul writing is also possible when pronunciation needs to be shown directly.

The alphabets (jamo)

There are a total of 41 alphabets (jamo) in Tangliengim, its alphabetical order is:
ㄱ ㄲ ㄴ ㄷ ㄸ ㄹ ㅁ ㅂ ㅃ ㅅ ㅇ ㅈ ㅉ ㅊ ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅎ ㆆ
ㅏ ᅟᅷ ㅐ ㅑ ᅟᆤ ㅓ ㅔ ㅕ ㅖ ㅗ ㅘ ㅙ ㅚ ㅛ ㅜ ㅞ ㅟ ㅠ ㅡ ᅟힻ ㅢ ㅣ

where ㅉ and ᅟힻ are only used in foreign words.

The order of the final letters is:
ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅀ ㅁ ㅂ ㅇ ㅎ

Romanisation

Main article: Tangliengim romanisation

Lomari is the romanised form of Tangliengim, representing the same pronunciation and tones as Tangliengim Hangul.

Final consonants

The audio pronounces the consonants along with the vowel “ㅏ (a)”.

Hangul Description
1 ㄱ
⟨-k⟩		 Final of 걱 (國 kork, like ‘ck’ in sick)
2 ㄴ
⟨-n⟩		 Final of 신ꞈ (新 sîn, like ‘n’ in sun)
3 ㄷ
⟨-t⟩		 Final of 닫ꞈ (值 tât, like ‘t’ in cat)
4 ㄹ
⟨-˷⟩		 Final of 귈ꞈ (關 kṵ̂i), indicates nasalised vowels³
5 ㅀ
⟨-˷h⟩		 Final of 햟 (挔 hia̰h)
(Combination of finals ㄹ + ㅎ)
Hangul Description
6 ㅁ
⟨-m⟩		 Final of 함ꞈ (蚶 hâm, like ‘m’ in hum)
7 ㅂ
⟨-p⟩		 Final of 찹 (插 chap, like ‘p’ in stop)
8 ㅇ
⟨-ng⟩		 Final of 성ˎ (爽 sòng, like ‘ng’ in song)⁴

³ ㄹ represents /l/ as an initial consonant but marks a nasal sound /◌̃/ in final position.
⁴ ㅇ is null in the initial position but represents the nasal sound /ŋ/ in the final position in place of ㆆ, which is only used as an initial consonant.

Tones

Hokkien is a tonal language, like Mandarin and Cantonese, where pitch distinguishes meaning. Tangliengim represents Hokkien with five tones.

Tone sandhi

Main article: Tone sandhi in Hokkien

In Hokkien, non-final characters undergo tone change (sandhi), as shown in the example “東方덩ˉ헝ˆ” here:

ꞈ 덩 tông

덩ꞈ is in citation tone as it is the final character.

ˍ 덩 tōng- ꞈ 헝 hông

덩ꞈ undergoes tone sandhi as a non-final character (덩ꞈ → 덩ˍ); meaning remains unchanged.

Original tone Changed tone

Tone sandhi is important in Hokkien, but beginners need not memorise it before reading Tangliengim, which writes tones in their changed forms where applicable.

Everyday phrases

Typing Tangliengim

Below is a quick guide to installing the input method (IME) on the computer. Since Unicode does not currently support tone diacritics, tones are omitted in everyday typing, but spacing rules still apply.

Using the standard Korean keyboard

For Windows 11 users,

  1. Under Settings > Time & Language > Language & Region > Options, select “Add a language” and add Korean.

As the standard Korean keyboard does not support the input of ᅟᅷ au and ᅟᆤ yau, which are frequently used in Hokkien, the official shorthand prescribed here are ᅟᅡᆽ and ᅟᅣᆽ.

Using the Old Hangul keyboard

In order to type characters such as ᄀᅷ kau or ᅙᅡ nga, the Old Hangul keyboard is needed.

For Windows 11 users,

  1. After adding Korean, select ” ··· Language options”.
  2. Under “Installed keyboards”, select “Add a keyboard”.
  3. Select “Microsoft Old Hangul“.

Spelling guidelines

Main article: Spelling guidelines of Tangliengim

Standard variety

Taipei Hokkien is the principal reference variety of this orthography.

Regional variation is normally resolved in favour of Taipei Hokkien, with occasional principled exceptions arising from the orthography’s internal design.
